title: The 10 Best Cordless Tire Inflators
subtitle: Battery-powered tire inflators with auto shut-off for cars, trucks, bikes and balls, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A cordless tire inflator tops off a low tire in a minute or two with no gas station and no cord. Set the pressure, clamp it on, and it stops itself. We ranked 10 best-sellers on rating, review volume and features (dual battery and 12V power, ±1 PSI accuracy, a tool battery platform and high airflow). Small built-in-battery units fit a glovebox; tool-battery inflators from DEWALT, Milwaukee and CRAFTSMAN suit the garage. They run from about $24 for AstroAI's L7 to $144 for DEWALT's 3-way inflator.
data_source: Amazon product listings on the data_captured date. Prices, ratings and review counts change daily; check the listing before relying on a number.

buyers_guide.q: Will a cordless inflator fill a flat tire?
buyers_guide.a: Most will, slowly. Small pumps are built for top-offs and may need a recharge to fill a large tire from flat. High-flow units like the ETENWOLF S6 or a tool-battery inflator handle flats and truck tires better.
Car tires run 30-40 PSI and light trucks up to 80. 150 PSI only matters for road-bike tires. Airflow (CFM or L/min) decides how fast it fills.
Most are within ±2 PSI; the best are ±1. Check against a good handheld gauge once, then trust the auto shut-off.
Built-in battery inflators are small and fit a glovebox. Tool-battery inflators share packs with your drill and usually move more air, but they're bigger.

buyers_guide.q: Can I use it in cold weather?
buyers_guide.a: Yes, but batteries lose capacity in the cold. Keep a dual-power model that also plugs into the car's 12V socket for winter.
